title: Felix and the Horizon Revisited
premise: Wren Eriksen, a clone of a murdered investigator, arrives at Horizon Colony to close a case no one wants reopened and to record the colony's quiet collapse for an Earth that has stopped listening. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Wren discovers the flicker was a weapon test by the colony's ruling consortium — and that his original was killed for finding out. Carrying the dead man's final message, Wren must choose between loyalty to the colonists who sheltered him and the truth that could end the war between Earth and the Outer Belt. He broadcasts the message as Earth's last transmission loop closes, forcing both sides to stand down — at the cost of Horizon itself, which he evacuates and then lets go dark.
about_author: Vesper Brightwater is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics engineer who spent six years on remote station rotations before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about people who inherit other people's unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Wren Eriksen docks at dying Horizon Colony carrying his original's unsolved murder file. POV: Wren. The colonists greet him with grief and suspicion — he wears a dead man's face. Emotional beat: displacement; Wren realizes he is investigating himself, or the man he was made from.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; ships drift, water rises, a child nearly dies. POV: alternating Wren and station engineer Mara Quill. Emotional beat: dread — this wasn't an accident, and everyone quietly knows it but no one will say so.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Filed
chapters.summary: Wren decrypts his original's hidden notes: survey data proving the consortium is strip-mining Horizon's core, causing the flicker tests. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cold clarity hardening into purpose as he understands why the original had to die.

chapters.title: Loyalty of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Mara shelters Wren when consortium security sweeps the colony; the community feeds him, lies for him, buries evidence in their gardens. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: belonging — Wren, designed to be no one's, is claimed by these people, complicating everything.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Offer
chapters.summary: Director Sef Askeland offers Wren the original's rank, home, and life — if he declares the case closed. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: temptation; the offer is genuinely kind, which makes it worse. He almost says yes.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Wren learns Earth's transmission loop goes permanently silent in eleven days; after that, no message can reach either war fleet. POV: Mara intercepting fleet chatter. Emotional beat: ticking-clock panic — the truth has a deadline now.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Consortium agents raid the colony for the notes; a neighbor dies covering Wren's escape. The community splits — some want the truth buried to survive the war. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt and rage; loyalty and truth begin tearing him apart.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: In the original's hidden lab, Wren finds the full recording: proof the flicker weapon was built to be used on Earth itself. The message must go to both fleets simultaneously or it starts the war instead. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: resolve forged from ruin.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren fights through the blackout to the relay array while Askeland begs him to stop — broadcasting means Horizon loses its shield of obscurity. He transmits as the loop's final seconds tick away. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terrible commitment; there is no version where he keeps everyone.

chapters.title: Horizon Revisited
chapters.summary: Both fleets stand down; the war ends not with victory but with shared shame. The colony evacuates under Earth's flag, its name becoming shorthand for what was nearly done. Wren stays behind to seal the records, finally at peace with borrowed bones. POV: Wren, coda. Emotional beat: mourning and release — survival was never free, but it was worth the price.
